parameters_and_allowed_inputs.notes: The complete public __signature_P (type-Check.lean:368–370), rather than a private preflight declaration, quantifies n:ℕ and E:Set(Ambient n), then exactly E.Nonempty and IsCompact E. These match both source parameters and H001/H002; n=0 is included. There are no external E propositions, extra project hypotheses, measurable-set premises, positive-dimension premises or public finiteness assumptions. Auxiliary metric spaces remain arbitrary, including empty spaces where the source permits them. Nonemptiness in N104/N105 is an implication on A, not an additional global instance. The internal hypotheses of T014 have explicit producer nodes; none becomes a public assumption. The private False preflight binders provide connection checks only and are not interpreted as premises or completed proofs.

representations_and_conversion_obligatio.notes: Checked the actual pinned definitions: EuclideanSpace k ι is PiLp 2 (fun _ : ι => k), with the square-root sum-of-squares norm; Fin n is the coordinate index type. WithLp has only its underlying-value construction field, not a hidden theorem field. The native product distance is max of component distances. Consequently Ambient, unitInterval, appendCoord and ×ˢ represent precisely the specified objects. Coordinate restriction to castSucc and evaluation at last invert appendCoord in both orders, also for n=0; T012 explicitly requires bijectivity and both distance bounds, and T013 requires dimension preservation for every subset. The source-to-image correspondence therefore works both ways without assuming norm invariance. H installs the canonical Borel structure definitionally, and the pinned native hausdorffMeasure_apply has exactly the guarded cover infimum used by Content. T003/T004 explicitly require the positive-exponent removal of the empty-member guard and the positive finite-scale supremum conversion. Native dimH uses nonnegative real exponents and this Borel Hausdorff measure. ENNReal real powers, ofReal and toReal have the stated endpoint conventions; s,q>0 and finite diameter bounds justify the planned real/ENNReal conversions. Product finiteness is proved before reversing toReal. The public finiteness conjuncts match the source and make the ENNReal and finite-real equalities equivalent in both directions. No target property is inserted into a definition.

However the required source-specific generic application records are missing: every recorded generic use has args:[] and merely reasserts the entire universal input type. In particular T014's T011 record fixes only universe 0; it does not apply N105 to Ambient n and E or supply H001 and T001's finiteness projection, as R107 explicitly does. result.value: Return to the original natural n and E⊆Ambient n. H001 gives that E is nonempty. N004 gives dimH E≤n and dimH E≠∞, including n=0. Instantiate N105 with X=Ambient n and A=E. Its nonemptiness and finite-dimension conditions are exactly these two available facts. It yields dimH(E×I)=dimH E+1 in MaxProd(Ambient n), and finiteness of that product dimension. Now apply N106 to the subset E×I. Under the fixed coordinate identification, appendCoord(n) '' (E×I) is precisely the original E×[0,1] in Euclidean ℝ^(n+1): its first n coordinates belong to E and its last coordinate belongs to [0,1], and conversely every such vector has this preimage. N106 transfers the maximum-metric dimension to this Euclidean image. Therefore dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 with the stipulated Euclidean metric. Both sides are finite by N004 and N105, so their [0,∞] equality is the equality of finite real dimensions as well. This proves P. The original compactness hypothesis remains retained but is unused in this strengthened basis route.

value.representation_notes: Keep the exact prepared YuiBasis header as prefix. Ambient n is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n): Fin n is the coordinate index type, and EuclideanSpace is PiLp 2, so 2 is the norm exponent, not a dimension parameter. Native X×ℝ has the maximum metric (Prod.dist_eq); set products are Set.prod (×ˢ). appendCoord uses Fin.lastCases to put t at Fin.last n and x_i at i.castSucc, with WithLp.toLp 2 selecting the target Euclidean norm. T012/T013 prove the actual metric conversion. H s A is the native unnormalized hausdorffMeasure on the canonical Borel sigma algebra of each metric space, with the BorelSpace equality witnessed definitionally; it adds no regularity assumption. C s δ A is exactly prepared Content s (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A. ENNReal.ofReal embeds max(δ,0), and only positive real scales occur in content assertions. Metric.ediam, infima, suprema, sums, dimensions and costs take values in ℝ≥0∞, retaining ∞; ^ on extended diameters is ENNReal real power, while ^ on real budgets is Real.rpow before ofReal. Positive exponents make empty costs zero. dimH uses Borel Hausdorff measure and nonnegative critical exponents intrinsically. Finite-dimensional and finite-product results imply that the final ENNReal equality is also equality of real dimensions. All H premises and N/P outputs are kept; no E exists here, no M port is needed, and reviewed background notes introduce no assumptions.

steps.explanation: Construct the inverse of appendCoord by reading the first n coordinates and the last coordinate. Split the sum of n+1 squares to obtain a²+b². Compare it to max(a,b)² and 2·max(a,b)², and take nonnegative square roots. This proves bijectivity and both explicit metric bounds, hence the stated Lipschitz and antilipschitz properties; Real.toNNReal sqrt(2) represents the nonnegative finite constant sqrt(2). The empty sum covers n=0.

1: import Mathlib
2: open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
3: open MeasureTheory MeasureTheory.Measure Set Metric
4: namespace YuiBasis
5: noncomputable def Content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
6:     (s : ℝ) (δ : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
7:   ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ δ),
8:     ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), Metric.ediam (U i) ^ s
9: abbrev Ambient (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
10: def unitInterval : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
11: noncomputable def appendCoord (n : ℕ) (p : Ambient n × ℝ) : Ambient (n + 1) :=
12:   WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.lastCases p.2 (fun i => p.1 i))
13: end YuiBasis
14: 
15: open YuiBasis
16: namespace YuiPlan
17: noncomputable def H {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
18:   letI : MeasurableSpace X := borel X
19:   letI : BorelSpace X := ⟨rfl⟩
20:   hausdorffMeasure s A
21: noncomputable def C {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
22:   YuiBasis.Content s (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A
23: end YuiPlan
24: open YuiPlan
25: namespace YuiPortTypes
26: abbrev T001 (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YuiBasis.Ambient n)) : Prop :=
27:   (0 ≤ dimH E ∧ dimH E ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞)) ∧ dimH E ≠ ⊤
28: abbrev T002 (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YuiBasis.Ambient n)) : Prop :=
29:   dimH YuiBasis.unitInterval = 1
30: abbrev T003.{u} (n : ℕ) (E : Set (YuiBasis.Ambient n)) : Prop :=
31:   ∀ (X : Type u) [MetricSpace X] (A : Set X) (s : ℝ), 0 < s →
32:   (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ →
33:     C s δ A = ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i)
34:       (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ), ∑' i, Metric.ediam (U i) ^ s) ∧
35:   (∀ δ₁ δ₂ : ℝ, 0 < δ₁ → δ₁ ≤ δ₂ → C s δ₂ A ≤ C s δ₁ A) ∧
36:   H s A = ⨆ (δ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < δ), C s δ A

value.representation_notes: Keep the exact prepared YuiBasis header as prefix. Native X×ℝ has the maximum metric (Prod.dist_eq); set products are Set.prod (×ˢ). appendCoord uses Fin.lastCases to put t at Fin.last n and x_i at i.castSucc, with WithLp.toLp 2 selecting the target Euclidean norm. T012/T013 prove the actual metric conversion. H s A is the native unnormalized hausdorffMeasure on the canonical Borel sigma algebra of each metric space, with the BorelSpace equality witnessed definitionally; it adds no regularity assumption. C s δ A is exactly prepared Content s (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A. ENNReal.ofReal embeds max(δ,0), and only positive real scales occur in content assertions. Positive exponents make empty costs zero. dimH uses Borel Hausdorff measure and nonnegative critical exponents intrinsically. import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
open MeasureTheory MeasureTheory.Measure Set Metric
namespace YuiBasis
noncomputable def Content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (δ : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ δ),
    ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), Metric.ediam (U i) ^ s
abbrev Ambient (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
def unitInterval : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
noncomputable def appendCoord (n : ℕ) (p : Ambient n × ℝ) : Ambient (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.lastCases p.2 (fun i => p.1 i))
end YuiBasis

open YuiBasis
namespace YuiPlan
noncomputable def H {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (s : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  letI : MeasurableSpace X := borel X
  letI : BorelSpace X := ⟨rfl⟩
  hausdorffMeasure s A
noncomputable def C {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (s δ : ℝ) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  YuiBasis.Content s (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A
end YuiPlan
open YuiPlan

P.explanation: The public parameters n:ℕ (including zero) and E:Set(EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) range over exactly the original Euclidean spaces and arbitrary subsets; E.Nonempty and IsCompact E preserve both original hypotheses. unitInterval=Icc 0 1. Fin.lastCases concatenates the n coordinates and final real coordinate, so appendCoord n '' (E×ˢunitInterval) is exactly the original subset E×[0,1] of Euclidean ℝ^(n+1), in both directions by reading those coordinates. The target states its Hausdorff dimension equals dimH E+1 and explicitly asserts both dimensions are finite. dimH is Mathlib's [0,∞]-valued critical-exponent dimension for the same unnormalized Hausdorff construction; for finite values the ENNReal equality is equivalent in both directions to the real-dimension equality. Compactness is retained even though the accepted basis proof does not use it. No n>0, measurability, positive dimension or further regularity premise is added.

value.full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
value.conclusion: With the stipulated Euclidean metrics and identification ℝ^n×ℝ=ℝ^(n+1), dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH(E)+1; equivalently dimH(appendCoord(n) '' (E×I))=dimH(E)+1. Both dimensions are finite, so this is also the equality of their real values.

definitions.type: ℕ → real finite dimensional inner product spaces
definitions.definition: Ambient(m)=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), the space of m real coordinates with norm ‖x‖₂=(Σ_{j<m}|x_j|²)^(1/2). The sum is zero when m=0. Distances are norms of differences. More generally the native EuclideanSpace k (Fin m), for a real-or-complex-like field k, is the m-coordinate k-space with this same sum-of-squared-absolute-values norm; its scalar vector-space structure is coordinatewise.

binders.type: vector in the indicated real or k-valued coordinate space

definitions.type: extended diameter of a subset of any pseudo extended metric space
definitions.definition: For a pseudo extended metric space Z and B⊆Z, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y):x∈B,y∈B} in [0,∞], with supremum of the empty set zero. For finite ediam, diam(B)=(ediam B).toReal and ediam B=ofReal(diam B). In metric spaces edist is ofReal of the ordinary distance.
ofReal(v) is max(v,0) embedded in the extended nonnegative reals. The notation z.toReal for z∈[0,∞] is its real value when finite, and zero for z=∞.

definitions.type: real exponent × extended scale × subset of an extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For an extended metric space Z, exponent u∈ℝ, scale h∈[0,∞], and B⊆Z, Content(u,h,B)=inf_{U:ℕ→Set Z; B⊆⋃_i U_i; ∀i ediam(U_i)≤h} Σ_i sup_{(_ : U_i nonempty)} (ediam U_i)^u. Infima, suprema and sums are in [0,∞]; an infimum over no covers is ∞. This is exactly the Content in basis-registry.json /lean_header. Countable covers may be padded by empty sets.
C_u(h,B), also written C_u(h,B), means Content(u,ofReal h,B) for real scale h. We use it only at h>0.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.type: real exponent × subset of a Borel extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: H^u(B)=μH[u](B) denotes Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure, the metric measure mkMetric for the gauge r↦r^u on the Borel sigma algebra. The metric-measure construction takes countable-cover outer contents for this gauge, with the empty-set gauge cost forced to zero, and their supremum as the scale tends to zero. Its precise cover evaluation will be applied as an explicit native source, rather than assumed as an extra premise. No spherical or dimensional normalization factor is used.

binders.type: subset of a Borel extended metric space

definitions.type: subset of an extended metric space → [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For B in an extended metric space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure when computing H, dimH(B)=sup{d∈[0,∞): H^d(B)=∞}, the supremum taken in [0,∞] and with sup ∅=0. This is native Mathlib dimH. Positive-exponent critical-exponent directions are invoked as explicit native sources. We use no zero-exponent measure assertion.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.definition: I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}. This is unitInterval in the basis header.

For a metric space Z, MaxProd(Z)=Z×ℝ with distance d_max((x,t),(y,u))=max(d_Z(x,y),|t−u|). For B⊆Z, B×I always denotes a subset of MaxProd(Z) in intermediate lemmas. All metric spaces in integration or Hausdorff-measure statements carry their Borel sigma algebra.

appendCoord(m)(x,t) is the vector whose first m coordinates are those of x and whose last coordinate is t. In the exact basis header it is WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.lastCases t (fun j => x j)). Its target always carries the Euclidean norm; its source here carries the maximum metric. It is a total coordinate construction, including m=0. Under the problem's identification ℝ^n×ℝ=ℝ^(n+1), the Euclidean set E×[0,1] is appendCoord(n) '' (E×I).

definitions.type: measure on the Borel sets of ℝ
definitions.definition: volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, with its usual Borel measurable structure (and its extension as an outer measure on arbitrary sets). Thus measure monotonicity applies to all subsets; no measurability of a covering set is implicit.
For a set B⊆Z and a scalar c∈[0,∞], c1_B denotes the function equal to c on B and zero off B, that is B.indicator(fun _ => c). This is meaningful for c=∞ as well, with no subtraction of infinities.

For a measurable space Z, measure μ and f:Z→[0,∞], ∫⁻ f dμ (the lower Lebesgue integral, lintegral) is the supremum of ∫g dμ over measurable nonnegative simple functions g≤f; a simple function integral is its finite sum of values times the measures of the corresponding disjoint level sets. All integrals in the slicing proof are lower integrals; integrability is never required.

binders.type: nonnegative measurable simple function on Z

definitions.type: nonnegative real × map of pseudo extended metric spaces → propositions
definitions.definition: LipschitzWith(K,f) means ∀x,y, edist(f x,f y)≤K·edist(x,y), where K is a finite nonnegative real embedded into [0,∞]. On metric spaces this is the usual distance inequality.

binders.type: map between pseudo extended metric spaces

definitions.type: nonnegative real × map of extended metric spaces → propositions
definitions.definition: AntilipschitzWith(L,f) means ∀x,y, edist(x,y)≤L·edist(f x,f y), with finite L≥0. On metric spaces this is the corresponding ordinary distance inequality.

definitions.type: ordered field or real vector space × endpoints → subsets
definitions.definition: segment(k,x,y)={a•x+b•y: a,b∈k, a≥0,b≥0,a+b=1}, in a vector space over an ordered scalar field k; over ℝ this is the usual closed line segment.

finrank(k,Z) is the dimension as a natural number of a finite-dimensional k-vector space Z (and is zero by the native total convention if the vector-space rank is infinite). In this proof its arguments are finite dimensional.

definitions.type: real or extended nonnegative base × real exponent → corresponding scalars
definitions.definition: The notation v^u uses the standard real power; on positive real v it is exp(u log v), with 0^u=0 for u>0 and 0^0=1. For extended nonnegative bases it is the usual extension: at u>0, ∞^u=∞ and 0^u=0; at u=0 the value is 1; at u<0, 0^u=∞ and ∞^u=0. Only nonnegative real bases and positive exponents occur in the covering calculations. The native real function at negative v is defined using |v|, as in Real.rpow.

R004.fact: For every natural n, the real coordinate space Ambient n with its given Euclidean inner product and norm is a finite-dimensional real normed vector space. Its coordinate vectors e_j, j∈Fin n, form a basis, including the empty basis for n=0; its metric also supplies an extended metric.

grounds.reason: n is a natural number, including zero, so Fin n is finite.
Ambient n is the real coordinate space with coordinatewise vector operations and its Euclidean inner product/norm.

R004.justification: Define e_j to have coordinate 1 at j and 0 elsewhere. Each x equals the finite sum Σ_j x_j e_j by evaluation at each coordinate. If Σ_j a_j e_j=0, evaluation at j gives a_j=0, proving independence. For n=0 every vector is the unique empty tuple, and spanning and independence hold for the empty family. Hence the space is finite dimensional. The supplied Euclidean inner product induces the displayed norm and the compatible real normed-space structure. Regard each finite real distance as an extended nonnegative distance to obtain the extended metric, preserving the metric axioms.

R005.fact: The real numbers with norm |x| and their usual addition and real scalar multiplication form a finite-dimensional real normed vector space, of dimension one, with basis consisting of 1.

grounds.reason: S001 explicitly takes the ambient space to be ℝ, with the standard real normed-space interpretation.
The supplied M012 statement requires the ambient real normed space to be finite dimensional; the present routine verification supplies precisely this condition for ℝ.

R005.justification: The real field operations give the real vector-space and additive-group laws. Absolute value is nonnegative, vanishes exactly at zero, is subadditive, and satisfies |a x|=|a||x|, so it gives the stated compatible norm. Every real x equals x·1, and a·1=0 implies a=0. Thus the singleton 1 spans and is linearly independent, proving finite dimensionality.

R101.fact: For the D004 infimum, enlarging the allowed scale decreases Content. Its supremum over positive extended scales equals its supremum over scales ofReal δ with real δ>0.

grounds.reason: Admissibility is the diameter upper bound; the value is an infimum in [0,∞].
The proof gives a positive finite δ with ofReal δ≤h for every positive extended h.

R101.justification: Every cover allowed at a smaller scale is allowed at a larger scale, so the larger-scale infimum is no greater. Each positive real scale occurs among the extended scales. Conversely each extended-scale content is bounded above by the content at the displayed smaller positive real scale. Taking suprema gives both inequalities.

R101.fact: If an infimum of admissible cover costs in [0,∞] equals zero, then for every real t>0 an admissible cover has cost <ofReal t.

grounds.reason: F001 expresses H as a supremum of nonnegative real-scale contents.
L2 gives H=0 and r,ε>0; hence the content at r/2 is zero and t=ε/4 is positive.

R101.justification: Each content is bounded above by the zero supremum and below by zero. If no admissible cost were below ofReal t, that positive number would be a lower bound for all costs, contradicting infimum zero. The empty family has infimum ∞, so cannot be the family here.

R101.fact: If z≤ofReal(r/2) with real r>0, then z is finite, d=z.toReal satisfies 0≤d≤r/2 and z=ofReal d. For s>0, (ofReal d)^s=ofReal(d^s).

grounds.reason: D002 supplies finite-diameter conversion.
D003 defines the finite embedding and toReal.
D018 specifies the corresponding real and extended powers.
F002 bounds every diameter by ofReal(r/2).

R101.justification: The upper bound is finite, so toReal is the inverse order-preserving real coordinate and gives the stated bounds. At d=0 both powers are zero since s>0. At d>0 both use the same positive real power, and the embedding preserves its value. This verifies the termwise cost conversion.

R101.fact: For ε>0 and e_i=ε·2^(−i−3), each e_i>0 and the real and extended nonnegative sums equal ε/4 and ofReal(ε/4), respectively.

grounds.reason: L2 gives ε>0.
S003 defines e and displays its finite partial sum (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)).

R101.justification: The displayed finite geometric identity follows by multiplying the partial sum by 1−1/2. The sequence 2^(−m) tends to zero (for example 2^m≥m+1 gives the elementary reciprocal bound). Thus the nonnegative partial sums increase to ε/4. Their supremum is the extended nonnegative sum, yielding the same finite embedded value.

R101.fact: For every i, continuity of x↦x^s at d_i, e_i>0 and d_i<r yield a_i with d_i<a_i<r and a_i^s<d_i^s+e_i; these choices may be made as a sequence.

grounds.reason: M020 supplies continuity once s≥0.
L1 gives s>0.
F003 supplies the real d_i, e_i>0, and d_i<r.

R101.justification: Continuity gives a radius ρ_i>0 for error e_i. Take η_i=(1/2)min(ρ_i,r−d_i)>0. Then η_i<ρ_i and η_i<r−d_i, so a_i=d_i+η_i has the claimed interval and power bounds. Ordinary countable choice of the established nonempty radius choices produces the sequence, as explicitly used in S004; no uniform radius or enlarged covering set is needed.

R101.fact: For nonnegative real sequences b_i,c_i,f_i with f_i≤b_i+c_i and finite totals B=Σ_i ofReal b_i, C=Σ_i ofReal c_i, one has Σ_i ofReal f_i≤B+C. In this application B<ofReal(ε/4), C=ofReal(ε/4), hence the budget total is <ofReal ε.

grounds.reason: F003 gives nonnegative d_i, positive errors, the bound on the original total and the finite error total.
F004 gives positive a_i and a_i^s<d_i^s+e_i.
s>0 ensures all these real powers are nonnegative.

R101.justification: For every finite initial segment, monotonicity and finite addition give the corresponding sum bound. Nonnegative series are suprema of these partial sums. The partial sums of b and c increase to their finite totals, so their sums increase to B+C; taking suprema proves the claimed weak bound. With b_i=d_i^s, c_i=e_i and f_i=a_i^s, finite scalar addition and ε>0 give B+C<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. No interchange involving signed terms or infinite strict addition is used.

R102.fact: If d is an extended nonnegative real, delta is a finite nonnegative real and d<=ofReal(delta), then d is finite, 0<=d.toReal<=delta and ofReal(d.toReal)=d. For finite nonnegative reals a,b, ofReal(a)<=ofReal(b) is equivalent to a<=b.

The order-preserving identification of the finite nonnegative part with the nonnegative real half-line gives the two inequalities and inverse conversion. This also permits passing from a pointwise edist bound to the real absolute-distance bound used in S002.

R102.fact: The real numbers with their usual order and metric bornology form an order bornology: metric-bounded sets are order-bounded, and every interval with finite real endpoints is metric-bounded. Thus the real structure satisfies the structural order/bornology premise of M018.

If 0<δ₁≤δ₂ then C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). Moreover H^s(A)=sup_{δ∈ℝ,δ>0} C_s(δ,A), so H agrees exactly with the unnormalized positive-exponent Hausdorff measure of problem.md. If H^s(A)=0, then for every r>0 and ε>0 there exist a natural-indexed cover U of A and real budgets a:ℕ→ℝ such that 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal(a_i), and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^s)<ofReal ε.

binders.type: metric space with Borel measurable structure

value.statement: For every metric space X, subset A⊆X, real s>0 and finite real δ>0, C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I) in the maximum product metric MaxProd(X). Consequently H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I), including infinite values. The slicing constant is exactly one; neither compactness nor measurability of A or its covers is required.

For every metric space X, A⊆X and real q>0, H^q(A)=0 implies H^{q+1}(A×I)=0 in MaxProd X. Under the same hypotheses q>0 and H^q(A)=0, for every target scale δ>0 and tolerance ε>0 there exists a natural-indexed cover of A×I whose members have extended diameter≤ofReal δ and whose total (q+1)-cost is <ofReal(2ε). The constant 2 is absolute, independent of X,A,δ,q.
For every metric space X and nonempty A⊆X, dimH(A×I)≥1 in the maximum metric MaxProd X.

For every metric space X and nonempty A⊆X with dimH(A)≠∞, the maximum product metric satisfies dimH(A×I)=dimH(A)+1 in [0,∞], and dimH(A×I)≠∞. Thus the corresponding finite real dimensions satisfy the same equality. No compactness or positive-dimension assumption is required.

The map appendCoord(n):MaxProd(Ambient n)→Ambient(n+1) is bijective and, for all p,p′ in its source, d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′). Thus it is √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz, and for every subset S⊆MaxProd(Ambient n), dimH(appendCoord(n) '' S)=dimH(S). Constants are independent of n and E. This includes n=0.

With the stipulated Euclidean metrics and identification ℝ^n×ℝ=ℝ^(n+1), dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH(E)+1; equivalently dimH(appendCoord(n) '' (E×I))=dimH(E)+1. Both dimensions are finite, so this is also the equality of their real values.

argument.text: Ambient n is the n-coordinate real inner product space, hence a finite-dimensional real normed vector space: its n coordinate vectors span and are independent, also for the empty coordinate family at n=0. Apply M008 to E⊆univ, M009 to this whole space, and M011 with scalar field ℝ and natural index n. This gives dimH E≤dimH(univ:Ambient n)=finrank(ℝ,Ambient n)=n. Nonnegativity is part of the [0,∞] codomain of dimH. M010 applied to E in the same space gives dimH E≠∞. No compactness or nonemptiness is used.

Every point of E belongs to univ.

argument.text: In the one-dimensional real normed space ℝ, 0≠1 and 0≤1. M012 gives dimH(segment(ℝ,0,1))=1; M013 gives segment(ℝ,0,1)=[0,1]=I. Substitution proves dimH I=1.

locals.type: metric space with its Borel measurable structure
locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X with its Borel sigma algebra.
Choose a cover U as in the earlier existence statement F002.
Choose the entire sequence of budgets a from F004 by countable choice.
For the antitone clause, let δ₁ be an arbitrary real scale.
Let δ₂ be an arbitrary real scale.
For the comparison of scale suprema, let h be any extended scale; the comparison is asserted for h>0.
For the positive-scale comparison define δ=h.toReal/2 when h<∞ and δ=1 when h=∞.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s, and assume L1: s>0. For an empty cover member, ediam ∅=0 and 0^s=0, so its guarded cost in Content is zero, exactly the raw diameter-power cost. For a nonempty member the supremum over its nonemptiness witnesses is that same power. Thus C_s is the stated raw countable-cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, each δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover; taking infima gives C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). Apply M001 at X,A,s. Its positive extended-scale supremum equals the positive finite real-scale supremum: every finite positive real scale is an allowed extended scale, while any h∈(0,∞] admits a finite real δ>0 with ofReal δ≤h (take δ=h.toReal/2 when h<∞, and δ=1 when h=∞). Scale antitonicity then bounds the content at h by the one at δ. This proves the normalization and supremum statements F001. The countable covers here are exactly those in problem.md; finite covers can be padded by empty sets.

produces.statement: For this X,A,s>0, C_s is the raw positive-exponent cover infimum, is antitone on positive scales, and H^s(A)=sup_{δ>0,δ∈ℝ} C_s(δ,A).

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real r,ε, and assume L2: H^s(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. F001 and nonnegativity give C_s(r/2,A)=0. The defining infimum then has a cover with cost <ofReal(ε/4): if no admissible cover had cost below that positive number, the infimum would be at least that number. In particular admissible covers exist; otherwise the infimum is ∞. This proves F002.

produces.statement: There exists U:ℕ→Set X covering A, with ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2) for every i and Σ_i (ediam U_i)^s<ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Choose U from F002, and define d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal and e_i=ε·2^(−i−3). Since ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2)<∞, we have 0≤d_i≤r/2<r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. Therefore the original cost is Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4). Each e_i is positive and Σ_i e_i=ε/4: the first m terms sum to (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), tending to ε/4. These finite partial sums also establish the corresponding extended-nonnegative sum identity.

produces.statement: U covers A; 0≤d_i≤r/2<r, ediam U_i=ofReal d_i, Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4), e_i>0 and Σ_i ofReal(e_i)=ofReal(ε/4).

argument.text: Use M020 with exponent s≥0. For each natural index i, continuity of x↦x^s at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r from F003 permit a positive η_i smaller than r−d_i and small enough that |(d_i+η_i)^s−d_i^s|<e_i. Indeed the continuity neighborhood for error e_i>0 contains an interval about d_i, and one can take half the minimum of its positive radius and r−d_i. Then d_i+η_i is in (d_i,r) and its s-power is <d_i^s+e_i. Countable choice of these individual values yields the sequence-existence statement F004; no covering sets are enlarged.

produces.statement: There exists a:ℕ→ℝ with d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^s<d_i^s+e_i for all natural i.

argument.text: Choose a from F004. By F003 and F004, 0<a_i≤r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i≤ofReal a_i. Comparing nonnegative finite partial sums and then their suprema gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^s)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)+Σ_i ofReal(e_i)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. Addition of these nonnegative sums is justified by the finite partial-sum identity and taking increasing suprema; all right-hand totals here are finite. This proves the required cover and positive budgets for every r,ε under L2. Discharge L2 into the stated implication, and discharge L1 into the positive-exponent universal statement. Together with F001 this proves all the claimed cover-content and positive-budget statements. Empty cover members received positive numerical budgets in the same way; the proof also works in singleton and zero-dimensional spaces.

applications.bindings: Source Z=X, real exponent u=s, subset B=A.
hypothesis_checks: X is the arbitrary metric space with its Borel sigma algebra; a metric is in particular an extended metric.

applications.bindings: Source q=s; evaluate continuity at each real d_i.
hypothesis_checks: L1 gives s>0, hence s≥0; F003 supplies finite nonnegative d_i, positive e_i and d_i<r for the actual choices.

locals.declaration: Fix any metric space X with its Borel sigma algebra.
Fix a finite real scale δ.
Fix an arbitrary sequence V of subsets of MaxProd X.
Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, including ρ_i=0 when V_i is empty.
Define Aproj_i as the projection of V_i to X.
Define Bproj_i as the projection of V_i to ℝ.
For each i define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] if V_i is nonempty, and J_i=∅ otherwise.
Define W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i and ∅ otherwise.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Fix an arbitrary sequence V and assume L2: V covers A×I and ediam V_i≤ofReal δ for every i. Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, Aproj_i=π_X(V_i), Bproj_i=π_ℝ(V_i). All ρ_i lie in [0,δ], and ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i. The two coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, since each coordinate distance is bounded by their maximum, the source distance. Applying M021 to each projection therefore gives ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. For empty V_i both projections and their diameters are empty and zero. This proves F001.

produces.statement: For every i, 0≤ρ_i≤δ, ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i, ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i, ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. Empty V_i have empty projections and ρ_i=0.

argument.text: Each Bproj_i is bounded in ℝ. If it is empty this is immediate. Otherwise, for any t_i∈Bproj_i, every t∈Bproj_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i by F001 and the defining diameter bound. Thus Bproj_i⊆[t_i−ρ_i,t_i+ρ_i], a bounded interval. This proves the boundedness statement F002 without choosing any measurable projection or any uniform center.

produces.statement: Every real projection Bproj_i is bounded.

argument.text: Define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] for nonempty V_i and J_i=∅ for empty V_i. For a nonempty index, M018 and F002 give Bproj_i⊆J_i, M017 gives ediam Bproj_i=ofReal(sup Bproj_i−inf Bproj_i), and M019 gives volume(J_i)=that same quantity≤ofReal ρ_i by F001. For empty indices inclusion and the zero volume bound are immediate. Every J_i is closed (or empty), hence Borel measurable; so is J_i∩I because I is closed. M019 at 0,1 also gives volume(I)=ofReal(1−0)=1. These are F003.

produces.statement: For every i, Bproj_i⊆J_i, J_i and J_i∩I are Borel measurable, and volume(J_i)≤ofReal ρ_i. Also I is Borel measurable and volume(I)=1; empty V_i give J_i=∅.

argument.text: Put c=C_s(δ,A) and W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i, otherwise ∅. For each t∈I these sets cover A: for any x∈A, the cover V contains (x,t) in some V_i, hence x∈Aproj_i and t∈Bproj_i⊆J_i by F003. Each W(t)_i has extended diameter≤ofReal δ by F001, and its s-cost is at most ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t), since s>0. N101's raw infimum formula yields c≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t). Define h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I}. On I the preceding inequality gives h≤Σ_i g_i; outside I both sides are zero. All g_i and h are Borel measurable: they take fixed constants on measurable sets and zero elsewhere, also when c=∞. This proves F004; we never require c to be finite.

produces.statement: h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I} are measurable nonnegative extended functions on ℝ, and h≤Σ_i g_i pointwise on ℝ.

argument.text:
Integrate the pointwise inequality of F004 with respect to volume on ℝ by M016. Apply M014 to the natural-indexed measurable family g, and M015 to h=c1_I and to each g_i. Using F003 and measure monotonicity gives
c=c·volume(I)=∫⁻h≤∫⁻Σ_i g_i=Σ_i∫⁻g_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i∩I)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) ofReal ρ_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^(s+1))=Σ_i(ediam V_i)^(s+1).
For ρ_i>0 the last power identity is ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1); for ρ_i=0 both s and s+1 are positive so both sides are zero. Empty indices also contribute zero. Measure monotonicity needs no additional measurability condition. Nonnegative sums are compared by finite partial sums and their suprema. These operations hold in [0,∞], with 0·∞=0 as usual; c·1=c even for c=∞. Since V was arbitrary, discharge L2 and universally quantify V. This is F005.

produces.statement: Every natural-indexed δ-cover V0 of A×I satisfies C_s(δ,A)≤Σ_i (ediam V0_i)^(s+1).

argument.text: Take the infimum of the cover costs in F005. N101 applies to exponent s+1>0 and gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I). This infimum argument is valid even if no δ-cover exists, in which case its right-hand infimum is ∞. The argument holds for every real δ>0. Take the supremum over these scales, and use N101 for both spaces and positive exponents s and s+1, to obtain H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s,δ. This proves the slicing inequality with constant one, for arbitrary subsets and without compactness.

applications.bindings: Z=MaxProd X, W=X, K=1, f=the first coordinate projection, subset V_i, for each i.
hypothesis_checks: The maximum metric and X are metric spaces, hence pseudo extended metric spaces; 1 is finite nonnegative.
For any pair of product points, their X-distance is at most the maximum of the two coordinate distances, so the projection is 1-Lipschitz.

applications.bindings: Z=MaxProd X, W=ℝ, K=1, f=the second coordinate projection, subset V_i, for each i.
hypothesis_checks: The maximum metric and the ordinary real metric give the required pseudo extended metrics; 1≥0.
The real coordinate distance is at most the maximum source distance.

applications.bindings: B=Bproj_i for each nonempty V_i.
hypothesis_checks: F002 proves boundedness of every Bproj_i from its finite diameter bound.

applications.bindings: Z=ℝ with its ordinary order and metric bornology, B=Bproj_i.
hypothesis_checks: The real conditionally complete linear order and its metric bornology are order compatible.
F002 proves boundedness for each Bproj_i.

applications.bindings: a=inf Bproj_i and b=sup Bproj_i for each nonempty V_i.
a=0 and b=1, so the interval is I.
Z=ℝ, μ=volume, f=h, and the upper function t↦Σ_i g_i(t).
hypothesis_checks: ℝ has its Borel measurable structure and volume is Lebesgue measure.
F004 proves the required pointwise inequality on all ℝ, including points outside I.

applications.bindings: Z=ℝ, μ=volume, T=ℕ, f_i=g_i.
hypothesis_checks: The domain is Borel ℝ with Lebesgue measure.
The indices are natural numbers, a countable type.
F004 proves every g_i Borel measurable, hence volume-a.e. measurable.

applications.bindings: Z=ℝ, μ=volume, B=I and the source constant c equal to the local c=C_s(δ,A).
hypothesis_checks: Borel ℝ and volume provide the measurable space and measure.
F003 proves I is Borel measurable; F004 defines h=c1_I.

applications.bindings: For every i, Z=ℝ, μ=volume, B=J_i∩I, and the source constant is ofReal(ρ_i^s).
hypothesis_checks: Borel ℝ and volume provide the measurable space and measure.
F003 proves all J_i∩I Borel measurable; F004 defines their weighted indicator functions g_i.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X.
Fix a real target scale δ.
Choose the cover component of the pair (U,a) whose existence is F001.
Choose the budget component a together with U from the same pair in F001.

argument.text: Fix X,A,q, and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Define r=min(1,δ)>0. N101, instantiated with s=q and this r,ε, gives existence of a pair consisting of a cover U of A and budgets a_i with 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε. Record this as F001 before choosing the pair.

produces.statement: There exist U:ℕ→Set X and a:ℕ→ℝ, chosen as one pair, such that U covers A, 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i, and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε.

argument.text:
Choose the pair (U,a) from F001. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i). Since 0<a_i≤r≤1, N_i≥1, 1/N_i≤a_i and N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Partition I by the N_i closed intervals Jpart_(i,j)=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] for 0≤j<N_i. The products Ppart_(i,j)=U_i×Jpart_(i,j) cover A×I. Distances within each product are bounded by max(a_i,1/N_i)≤a_i, so its extended diameter is ≤ofReal a_i≤ofReal δ. Their index set {(i,j): i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Thus the products can be reindexed as a natural sequence, with empty padding if necessary. Reindexing preserves the sum of nonnegative costs: both are suprema of the same finite subfamily sums. Their total (q+1)-cost satisfies
Σ_i Σ_{j<N_i}(ediam Ppart_(i,j))^(q+1)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(N_i a_i^(q+1))
 ≤Σ_i ofReal((2/a_i)a_i^(q+1))
 =2Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal(2ε).
All divisions are by positive a_i; real powers give a_i^(q+1)/a_i=a_i^q. This proves the countable-cover existence and cost bound F002, with absolute constant 2.

produces.statement: There exists a natural-indexed δ-cover of A×I in MaxProd X with total (q+1)-cost <ofReal(2ε).

argument.text: N101 identifies C_{q+1}(δ,A×I) with the cover-cost infimum. By F002 it is ≤ofReal(2ε) for every ε>0 at each fixed δ>0, so it is zero: any positive finite lower bound is contradicted by taking a smaller ε, and even one such finite bound excludes ∞. Discharge L2 to obtain the asserted existence for every δ,ε>0 and zero content for every δ>0. N101's finite-positive-scale supremum then yields H^{q+1}(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves both claimed clauses, including the scale/tolerance statement and its constant.
Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty. This says precisely that there exists a point x₀∈A, the existence recorded as F001.

produces.statement: There exists x₀∈X with x₀∈A.

argument.text: Choose x₀∈A from F001 and define f:ℝ→MaxProd X by f(t)=(x₀,t). For all real t,u, d_max(f(t),f(u))=max(d_X(x₀,x₀),|t−u|)=max(0,|t−u|)=|t−u|. Thus f is both 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz. Also f '' I⊆A×I, because x₀∈A. Record these facts as F002.

produces.statement: f is 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz from ℝ to MaxProd X, and f '' I⊆A×I.

argument.text: Apply M006 and M007 to f and I using F002; their two opposite image inequalities give dimH(f '' I)=dimH I. N005 says dimH I=1. Apply M008 in MaxProd X to the inclusion in F002, obtaining 1=dimH(f '' I)≤dimH(A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify X,A. This proves the claimed lower bound; the chosen point's identity is absent from the conclusion.

hypothesis_checks: Both source and target are metric spaces and K=1 is nonnegative.
F002 gives f 1-Lipschitz by the exact distance identity.

F002 gives f 1-antilipschitz by the same identity.

F002 proves f '' I⊆A×I from x₀∈A.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary metric space X with its Borel sigma algebra.
For the upper-bound contradiction define qmid=D0+(T0−D0−1)/2.
For the lower-bound contradiction define smid=(max(0,T0−1)+D0)/2.

argument.text: Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty and dimH A≠∞. Define D0=(dimH A).toReal and G=A×I. Since dimH A is finite and nonnegative, D0≥0 and ofReal D0=dimH A. This establishes F001 and legitimately permits approximation by real exponents.

produces.statement: D0≥0, ofReal D0=dimH A, A is nonempty, and G=A×I in MaxProd X.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary real q and assume L2: q>D0. Then q>0 by F001. Instantiate M003 with subset A and nonnegative exponent q: ofReal q>dimH A, so H^q(A)=0. N103 with X,A,q yields H^{q+1}(G)=0. Record this exact measure conclusion as F002.

Apply M004 in MaxProd X to G and exponent q+1>0, using F002's zero measure (zero≠∞). It gives dimH G≤ofReal(q+1). Since q was arbitrary, discharge L2 into the complete universally quantified assertion F003.

produces.statement: For every real q0>D0, dimH G≤ofReal(q0+1).

argument.text: Take q0=D0+1 in F003; the resulting finite upper bound proves dimH G≠∞. Define T0=(dimH G).toReal, so T0≥0 and ofReal T0=dimH G. To prove the sharp upper bound, assume L3: T0>D0+1, and define qmid=D0+(T0−D0−1)/2. Then qmid>D0 and qmid+1<T0. F003 at qmid gives T0≤qmid+1, a contradiction. Discharge L3 by classical contradiction, obtaining T0≤D0+1. Independently, N104 applies to the nonempty A from F001 and gives dimH G≥1, hence T0≥1. These finite-dimension and bound facts are F004.

produces.statement: dimH G≠∞, T0≥1, ofReal T0=dimH G, and T0≤D0+1.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary real s and assume L4: 0<s<D0. By F001, ofReal s<dimH A. M002 at subset A and nonnegative exponent s gives H^s(A)=∞, the exact assertion F005.

produces.statement: s>0 and H^s(A)=∞.

argument.text: Instantiate N102 with X,A,s. Since s>0, F005 and its measure inequality give ∞=H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I)=H^{s+1}(G), so H^{s+1}(G)=∞. This is F006.
Apply M005 in MaxProd X at subset G and exponent s+1, using F006. It gives ofReal(s+1)≤dimH G, hence s+1≤T0 by F004. Discharge L4 and quantify the arbitrary s to obtain F007.

produces.statement: For every real s0 with 0<s0<D0, s0+1≤T0.

argument.text: By D0≥0 from F001, the cases D0=0 and D0>0 are exhaustive. In the first branch assume L5: D0=0. F004 gives T0≥1=D0+1; close this branch and discharge L5. In the second branch assume L6: D0>0. To prove T0≥D0+1 assume L7: T0<D0+1 and define smid=(max(0,T0−1)+D0)/2. Both 0 and T0−1 are <D0, so max(0,T0−1)<smid<D0. In particular smid>0 and T0<smid+1, whereas F007 gives smid+1≤T0. This is a contradiction; discharge L7, obtaining T0≥D0+1 in this branch, and discharge L6. Case elimination therefore gives T0≥D0+1 universally. With F004's opposite bound, T0=D0+1. Since ofReal D0=dimH A and ofReal T0=dimH G, this is dimH(A×I)=dimH A+1 in [0,∞]. The finiteness clause is F004. Discharge L1 and quantify X,A; this proves the claimed dimension equality and finiteness, including the case D0=0.

hypothesis_checks: X is a metric space with its Borel measurable structure.
L2 and F001 give q>D0≥0 and ofReal q>dimH A.

hypothesis_checks: The maximum metric is a metric and we use its Borel sigma algebra.
F002 supplies q>0 and H^{q+1}(G)=0≠∞.

applications.bindings: Z=X, B=A, d=s as a nonnegative real.
hypothesis_checks: X is the fixed metric space with its Borel measurable structure.
L4 and F001 give 0<s<D0 and hence ofReal s<dimH A.

applications.bindings: Z=MaxProd X, B=G, d=s+1 as a nonnegative real.
hypothesis_checks: MaxProd X is metric and carries its Borel sigma algebra.
F006 supplies s+1>0 and H^{s+1}(G)=∞.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary source point p.
Fix another arbitrary source point p′.
Fix an arbitrary subset S of the maximum-metric product.

argument.text:
The map appendCoord(n) places the n coordinates of its first component before its real second component. Its inverse reads off these first n coordinates and the last coordinate. These coordinate operations are inverse in both orders, so the map is bijective. Fix arbitrary source points p,p′ and put a=‖p.1−p′.1‖₂≥0, b=|p.2−p′.2|≥0. Splitting the finite sum of squares into the first n terms and the last term gives
 d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)^2
   =Σ_{i<n}|p.1_i−p′.1_i|²+|p.2−p′.2|²=a²+b².
Since max(a,b)²≤a²+b²≤2max(a,b)², taking nonnegative square roots gives
 d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p,appendCoord(n)p′)≤√2·d_max(p,p′).
The maximum is exactly the source distance. Quantifying p,p′, these inequalities establish √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz bounds. When n=0, the coordinate sum is empty and zero, the first component is the unique vector of Ambient 0, and the same inverse and estimates still apply. Record the full construction and bounds as F001.

produces.statement: appendCoord(n):MaxProd(Ambient n)→Ambient(n+1) is bijective, is √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz, and its distances satisfy d_max(p0,p1)≤d₂(appendCoord(n)p0,appendCoord(n)p1)≤√2·d_max(p0,p1) for all source points p0,p1. This holds including n=0.

argument.text: Fix an arbitrary subset S⊆MaxProd(Ambient n). Apply M006 with map appendCoord(n) and K=√2≥0, using F001, to obtain dimH(appendCoord(n) '' S)≤dimH S. Apply M007 with the same map and L=1, again using F001, to obtain the reverse inequality. Antisymmetry gives equality for every S. Together with F001's bijectivity and the two explicit distance bounds, this proves the claimed metric bridge and dimension preservation. Both constants are absolute; no norm-invariance assertion is assumed.

applications.bindings: Z=MaxProd(Ambient n), W=Ambient(n+1), K=√2 as a nonnegative real, f=appendCoord(n), subset S.
hypothesis_checks: Both the maximum-product and target Euclidean metrics are metric spaces; √2 is finite and nonnegative.
F001 proves the upper distance bound for every pair, exactly the √2-Lipschitz premise.

applications.bindings: Z=MaxProd(Ambient n), W=Ambient(n+1), L=1, f=appendCoord(n), subset S.
hypothesis_checks: The same metric spaces supply extended metrics and 1 is nonnegative.
F001 proves d_max≤d₂ for every pair, exactly the 1-antilipschitz premise.

argument.text: Return to the original natural n and E⊆Ambient n. H001 gives that E is nonempty. N004 gives dimH E≤n and dimH E≠∞, including n=0. Instantiate N105 with X=Ambient n and A=E. Its nonemptiness and finite-dimension conditions are exactly these two available facts. It yields dimH(E×I)=dimH E+1 in MaxProd(Ambient n), and finiteness of that product dimension. Now apply N106 to the subset E×I. Under the fixed coordinate identification, appendCoord(n) '' (E×I) is precisely the original E×[0,1] in Euclidean ℝ^(n+1): its first n coordinates belong to E and its last coordinate belongs to [0,1], and conversely every such vector has this preimage. N106 transfers the maximum-metric dimension to this Euclidean image. Therefore dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 with the stipulated Euclidean metric. Both sides are finite by N004 and N105, so their [0,∞] equality is the equality of finite real dimensions as well. This proves P. The original compactness hypothesis remains retained but is unused in this strengthened basis route.

value.text: Ambient n is the n-coordinate real inner product space, hence a finite-dimensional real normed vector space: its n coordinate vectors span and are independent, also for the empty coordinate family at n=0. Apply M008 to E⊆univ, M009 to this whole space, and M011 with scalar field ℝ and natural index n. This gives dimH E≤dimH(univ:Ambient n)=finrank(ℝ,Ambient n)=n. Nonnegativity is part of the [0,∞] codomain of dimH. M010 applied to E in the same space gives dimH E≠∞. No compactness or nonemptiness is used.
In the one-dimensional real normed space ℝ, 0≠1 and 0≤1. M012 gives dimH(segment(ℝ,0,1))=1; M013 gives segment(ℝ,0,1)=[0,1]=I. Substitution proves dimH I=1.

Fix arbitrary X,A,s, and assume L1: s>0. For an empty cover member, ediam ∅=0 and 0^s=0, so its guarded cost in Content is zero, exactly the raw diameter-power cost. For a nonempty member the supremum over its nonemptiness witnesses is that same power. Thus C_s is the stated raw countable-cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, each δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover; taking infima gives C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). Apply M001 at X,A,s. Its positive extended-scale supremum equals the positive finite real-scale supremum: every finite positive real scale is an allowed extended scale, while any h∈(0,∞] admits a finite real δ>0 with ofReal δ≤h (take δ=h.toReal/2 when h<∞, and δ=1 when h=∞). Scale antitonicity then bounds the content at h by the one at δ. This proves the normalization and supremum statements F001. The countable covers here are exactly those in problem.md; finite covers can be padded by empty sets.

Fix arbitrary real r,ε, and assume L2: H^s(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. F001 and nonnegativity give C_s(r/2,A)=0. The defining infimum then has a cover with cost <ofReal(ε/4): if no admissible cover had cost below that positive number, the infimum would be at least that number. In particular admissible covers exist; otherwise the infimum is ∞. This proves F002.

Choose U from F002, and define d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal and e_i=ε·2^(−i−3). Since ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2)<∞, we have 0≤d_i≤r/2<r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. Therefore the original cost is Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)<ofReal(ε/4). Each e_i is positive and Σ_i e_i=ε/4: the first m terms sum to (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), tending to ε/4. These finite partial sums also establish the corresponding extended-nonnegative sum identity.

Use M020 with exponent s≥0. For each natural index i, continuity of x↦x^s at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r from F003 permit a positive η_i smaller than r−d_i and small enough that |(d_i+η_i)^s−d_i^s|<e_i. Indeed the continuity neighborhood for error e_i>0 contains an interval about d_i, and one can take half the minimum of its positive radius and r−d_i. Then d_i+η_i is in (d_i,r) and its s-power is <d_i^s+e_i. Countable choice of these individual values yields the sequence-existence statement F004; no covering sets are enlarged.

Choose a from F004. By F003 and F004, 0<a_i≤r and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i≤ofReal a_i. Comparing nonnegative finite partial sums and then their suprema gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^s)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^s)+Σ_i ofReal(e_i)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. Addition of these nonnegative sums is justified by the finite partial-sum identity and taking increasing suprema; all right-hand totals here are finite. This proves the required cover and positive budgets for every r,ε under L2. Discharge L2 into the stated implication, and discharge L1 into the positive-exponent universal statement. Together with F001 this proves all the claimed cover-content and positive-budget statements. Empty cover members received positive numerical budgets in the same way; the proof also works in singleton and zero-dimensional spaces.

Fix arbitrary X,A,s,δ and assume L1: s>0 and δ>0. Fix an arbitrary sequence V and assume L2: V covers A×I and ediam V_i≤ofReal δ for every i. Define ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, Aproj_i=π_X(V_i), Bproj_i=π_ℝ(V_i). All ρ_i lie in [0,δ], and ediam V_i=ofReal ρ_i. The two coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, since each coordinate distance is bounded by their maximum, the source distance. Applying M021 to each projection therefore gives ediam Aproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam Bproj_i≤ofReal ρ_i. For empty V_i both projections and their diameters are empty and zero. This proves F001.

Each Bproj_i is bounded in ℝ. If it is empty this is immediate. Otherwise, for any t_i∈Bproj_i, every t∈Bproj_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i by F001 and the defining diameter bound. Thus Bproj_i⊆[t_i−ρ_i,t_i+ρ_i], a bounded interval. This proves the boundedness statement F002 without choosing any measurable projection or any uniform center.

Define J_i=[inf Bproj_i,sup Bproj_i] for nonempty V_i and J_i=∅ for empty V_i. For a nonempty index, M018 and F002 give Bproj_i⊆J_i, M017 gives ediam Bproj_i=ofReal(sup Bproj_i−inf Bproj_i), and M019 gives volume(J_i)=that same quantity≤ofReal ρ_i by F001. For empty indices inclusion and the zero volume bound are immediate. Every J_i is closed (or empty), hence Borel measurable; so is J_i∩I because I is closed. M019 at 0,1 also gives volume(I)=ofReal(1−0)=1. These are F003.

Put c=C_s(δ,A) and W(t)_i=Aproj_i if t∈J_i, otherwise ∅. For each t∈I these sets cover A: for any x∈A, the cover V contains (x,t) in some V_i, hence x∈Aproj_i and t∈Bproj_i⊆J_i by F003. Each W(t)_i has extended diameter≤ofReal δ by F001, and its s-cost is at most ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t), since s>0. N101's raw infimum formula yields c≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t). Define h=c1_I and g_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I}. On I the preceding inequality gives h≤Σ_i g_i; outside I both sides are zero. All g_i and h are Borel measurable: they take fixed constants on measurable sets and zero elsewhere, also when c=∞. This proves F004; we never require c to be finite.

Integrate the pointwise inequality of F004 with respect to volume on ℝ by M016. Apply M014 to the natural-indexed measurable family g, and M015 to h=c1_I and to each g_i. Using F003 and measure monotonicity gives
c=c·volume(I)=∫⁻h≤∫⁻Σ_i g_i=Σ_i∫⁻g_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i∩I)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) ofReal ρ_i
 =Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^(s+1))=Σ_i(ediam V_i)^(s+1).
For ρ_i>0 the last power identity is ρ_i^s·ρ_i=ρ_i^(s+1); for ρ_i=0 both s and s+1 are positive so both sides are zero. Empty indices also contribute zero. Measure monotonicity needs no additional measurability condition. Nonnegative sums are compared by finite partial sums and their suprema. These operations hold in [0,∞], with 0·∞=0 as usual; c·1=c even for c=∞. Since V was arbitrary, discharge L2 and universally quantify V. This is F005.

Take the infimum of the cover costs in F005. N101 applies to exponent s+1>0 and gives C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I). This infimum argument is valid even if no δ-cover exists, in which case its right-hand infimum is ∞. The argument holds for every real δ>0. Take the supremum over these scales, and use N101 for both spaces and positive exponents s and s+1, to obtain H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I). Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,s,δ. This proves the slicing inequality with constant one, for arbitrary subsets and without compactness.

Fix X,A,q, and assume L1: q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix arbitrary real δ,ε and assume L2: δ>0 and ε>0. Define r=min(1,δ)>0. N101, instantiated with s=q and this r,ε, gives existence of a pair consisting of a cover U of A and budgets a_i with 0<a_i≤r, ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal ε. Record this as F001 before choosing the pair.

Choose the pair (U,a) from F001. Define N_i=ceil(1/a_i). Since 0<a_i≤r≤1, N_i≥1, 1/N_i≤a_i and N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i. Partition I by the N_i closed intervals Jpart_(i,j)=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i] for 0≤j<N_i. The products Ppart_(i,j)=U_i×Jpart_(i,j) cover A×I. Distances within each product are bounded by max(a_i,1/N_i)≤a_i, so its extended diameter is ≤ofReal a_i≤ofReal δ. Their index set {(i,j): i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Thus the products can be reindexed as a natural sequence, with empty padding if necessary. Reindexing preserves the sum of nonnegative costs: both are suprema of the same finite subfamily sums. Their total (q+1)-cost satisfies
Σ_i Σ_{j<N_i}(ediam Ppart_(i,j))^(q+1)
 ≤Σ_i ofReal(N_i a_i^(q+1))
 ≤Σ_i ofReal((2/a_i)a_i^(q+1))
 =2Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)<ofReal(2ε).
All divisions are by positive a_i; real powers give a_i^(q+1)/a_i=a_i^q. This proves the countable-cover existence and cost bound F002, with absolute constant 2.

N101 identifies C_{q+1}(δ,A×I) with the cover-cost infimum. By F002 it is ≤ofReal(2ε) for every ε>0 at each fixed δ>0, so it is zero: any positive finite lower bound is contradicted by taking a smaller ε, and even one such finite bound excludes ∞. Discharge L2 to obtain the asserted existence for every δ,ε>0 and zero content for every δ>0. N101's finite-positive-scale supremum then yields H^{q+1}(A×I)=0. Discharge L1 and universally quantify X,A,q. This proves both claimed clauses, including the scale/tolerance statement and its constant.
Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty. This says precisely that there exists a point x₀∈A, the existence recorded as F001.

Choose x₀∈A from F001 and define f:ℝ→MaxProd X by f(t)=(x₀,t). For all real t,u, d_max(f(t),f(u))=max(d_X(x₀,x₀),|t−u|)=max(0,|t−u|)=|t−u|. Thus f is both 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz. Also f '' I⊆A×I, because x₀∈A. Record these facts as F002.

Apply M006 and M007 to f and I using F002; their two opposite image inequalities give dimH(f '' I)=dimH I. N005 says dimH I=1. Apply M008 in MaxProd X to the inclusion in F002, obtaining 1=dimH(f '' I)≤dimH(A×I). Discharge L1 and quantify X,A. This proves the claimed lower bound; the chosen point's identity is absent from the conclusion.

Fix X,A and assume L1: A is nonempty and dimH A≠∞. Define D0=(dimH A).toReal and G=A×I. Since dimH A is finite and nonnegative, D0≥0 and ofReal D0=dimH A. This establishes F001 and legitimately permits approximation by real exponents.

Fix an arbitrary real q and assume L2: q>D0. Then q>0 by F001. Instantiate M003 with subset A and nonnegative exponent q: ofReal q>dimH A, so H^q(A)=0. N103 with X,A,q yields H^{q+1}(G)=0. Record this exact measure conclusion as F002.

Apply M004 in MaxProd X to G and exponent q+1>0, using F002's zero measure (zero≠∞). It gives dimH G≤ofReal(q+1). Since q was arbitrary, discharge L2 into the complete universally quantified assertion F003.

Take q0=D0+1 in F003; the resulting finite upper bound proves dimH G≠∞. Define T0=(dimH G).toReal, so T0≥0 and ofReal T0=dimH G. To prove the sharp upper bound, assume L3: T0>D0+1, and define qmid=D0+(T0−D0−1)/2. Then qmid>D0 and qmid+1<T0. F003 at qmid gives T0≤qmid+1, a contradiction. Discharge L3 by classical contradiction, obtaining T0≤D0+1. Independently, N104 applies to the nonempty A from F001 and gives dimH G≥1, hence T0≥1. These finite-dimension and bound facts are F004.
Fix an arbitrary real s and assume L4: 0<s<D0. By F001, ofReal s<dimH A. M002 at subset A and nonnegative exponent s gives H^s(A)=∞, the exact assertion F005.
Instantiate N102 with X,A,s. Since s>0, F005 and its measure inequality give ∞=H^s(A)≤H^{s+1}(A×I)=H^{s+1}(G), so H^{s+1}(G)=∞. This is F006.
Apply M005 in MaxProd X at subset G and exponent s+1, using F006. It gives ofReal(s+1)≤dimH G, hence s+1≤T0 by F004. Discharge L4 and quantify the arbitrary s to obtain F007.

By D0≥0 from F001, the cases D0=0 and D0>0 are exhaustive. In the first branch assume L5: D0=0. F004 gives T0≥1=D0+1; close this branch and discharge L5. In the second branch assume L6: D0>0. To prove T0≥D0+1 assume L7: T0<D0+1 and define smid=(max(0,T0−1)+D0)/2. Both 0 and T0−1 are <D0, so max(0,T0−1)<smid<D0. In particular smid>0 and T0<smid+1, whereas F007 gives smid+1≤T0. This is a contradiction; discharge L7, obtaining T0≥D0+1 in this branch, and discharge L6. Case elimination therefore gives T0≥D0+1 universally. With F004's opposite bound, T0=D0+1. Since ofReal D0=dimH A and ofReal T0=dimH G, this is dimH(A×I)=dimH A+1 in [0,∞]. The finiteness clause is F004. Discharge L1 and quantify X,A; this proves the claimed dimension equality and finiteness, including the case D0=0.

The map appendCoord(n) places the n coordinates of its first component before its real second component. Its inverse reads off these first n coordinates and the last coordinate. 1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.
168:

172: tests. It is a natural-language input, not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
173: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must independently produce
174: and check those artifacts. The basic Hausdorff-measure and integration facts
175: used here must be registered by that future NL0/Audit A workflow.

88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.

The same supremum is obtained from finite positive real scales: those are included in all extended scales, and every positive extended scale r admits a finite positive real δ with ofReal δ≤r, so its content is bounded by the content at δ. import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
open MeasureTheory MeasureTheory.Measure Set Metric
namespace YuiBasis
noncomputable def Content {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X]
    (s : ℝ) (δ : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ δ),
    ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (U i).Nonempty), Metric.ediam (U i) ^ s
abbrev Ambient (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
def unitInterval : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
noncomputable def appendCoord (n : ℕ) (p : Ambient n × ℝ) : Ambient (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.lastCases p.2 (fun i => p.1 i))
end YuiBasis
